issues.title: From Allie B. regarding S_REPLY
issues.author: csosto-pk
issues.body:
> Hey All! 
>      I have a question about draft-harrison-sshm-mlkem - in section 3 the new version states: 
> 
> The server sends SSH_MSG_KEX_KEM_REPLY.  With this, the server sends S_REPLY which is the concatenation of S_CT.
> 
> I think this is meant to be  'concatenation of S_CT with the server public host key (or certificate)', or something of that nature. 
> 
> Also, I can only find S_REPLY defined in the hybrid drafts, and while it makes sense to use here since you need to concat the ciphertext and public key to send in the reply message, I think it might be worth writing out the structure of SSH_MSG_KEX_KEM_REPLY and defining each component for clarity, like
>  
>     byte        SSH_MSG_KEX_KEM_REPLY 
>     string     K_S server's public host key 
>     string     S_REPLY 
>     string     signature of H
> 
> where S_REPLY is the concatenation of S_CT (the cipher txt output of the Encaps function) and K_S.

comments.author: csosto-pk
comments.body:
I think this is correct. The "concatenation" text was inadvertently pulled from the PQ-hybrid SSH draft. 

The existing text

> With this, the server sends S_REPLY  which is the concatenation of S_CT and S_PK. 

 needs to be updated to say that the reply should include the ML-KEM ciphertext produced from the encapsulation of the client ML-KEM public key. 

It would probably be nice to show it like the PQ-hybrid draft 

>          byte     SSH_MSG_KEX_HYBRID_INIT
>          string   C_INIT
> 
> where C_INIT is the ML-KEM ephemeral public key 

>          byte     SSH_MSG_KEX_HYBRID_REPLY
>          string   K_S, server's public host key
>          string   S_REPLY
>          string   the signature on the exchange hash
> 
> where S_REPLY is the ML-KEM ciphertext from the encapsulation to the client's ML-KEM ephemeral public key. 

I also suggest to remove ```SSH_MSG_KEXDH_INIT``` and just keep ```SSH_MSG_KEX_KEM_INIT```. 

> The client sends ~~SSH_MSG_KEXDH_INIT [RFC4253]~~ or SSH_MSG_KEX_KEM_INIT ~~[RFC5656]~~

pulls.title: Some fixes
pulls.author: csosto-pk
pulls.body:
I did not compile it. It may need to fix the references to compile. 

Please proof read. Also please check if OQS OpenSSH encodes K_PQ as mpint. Since it sia 256-bit value it could, it is not necessary to encode it as as a byte arraw because it is not the concatenation of two things. 

I would also suggest to consider dropping MLKEM-512, but since you have the IANA assignments, I guess you can keep it.

comments.body:

> 
> Please proof read. Also please check if OQS OpenSSH encodes K_PQ as mpint. Since it sia 256-bit value it could, it is not necessary to encode it as as a byte arraw because it is not the concatenation of two things.
>

It actually looks like it did not start this way (https://github.com/open-quantum-safe/openssh/issues/119), but was changed in 2022 here: https://github.com/open-quantum-safe/openssh/commit/e9b0f6f8896039824f78a43623cd14b67f24e2ce so I think we are good there.
Sorry, wrong reference here. It should be [draft-ietf-sshm-mlkem-hybrid-kex] instead of the NTRU one
